**Novelty (originality, unexpectedness): 5**
Why? The solution brilliantly subverts standard industry playbooks. Instead of defaulting to "more audits" and "higher inventory," it exposes why those metrics fail (e.g., dual-sourcing converging at tier-3, audits measuring coaching rather than harm). Proposing that the company audit its own purchasing practices, explicitly price "honesty" via disclosure protection, and treating rising worker grievances as a success metric are highly unexpected, paradigm-shifting approaches.

**Usefulness/Feasibility (practicality, implementability): 4.5**
Why? The ideas are highly practical and grounded in operational reality (e.g., PPAP timelines, credit insurer signals, engineering gate reviews). The author deliberately sequences low-cost, high-impact actions first. It loses a half-point only because some of the most transformative ideas—giving engineering a resilience veto and legally protecting problem-disclosing suppliers from volume loss—will face immense internal political resistance, making full implementation challenging.

**Flexibility (multiple approaches, adaptability): 5**
Why? The solution is inherently anti-dogmatic. It explicitly rejects rigid three-year roadmaps in favor of an agile, 90-day pilot approach. It frames its ideas as "bets" to put on the table rather than rigid mandates, adapts to the reality that the situation will change, and even includes a "What would tell me I'm wrong" section, showing a high degree of adaptability and intellectual flexibility.

**Elaboration (detail, development): 5**
Why? The proposal is exceptionally well-developed. It doesn't just state concepts; it provides the exact operational mechanisms required to execute them. For example, instead of just saying "improve traceability," it specifies "isotopic or genetic testing rather than paperwork" and tracing to the "smelter, mill, gin, refinery." It details the exact KPIs, contract clauses, and cross-functional team structures needed to make the strategies work.

**Cultural Sensitivity (cross-cultural appropriateness): 5**
Why? The solution demonstrates deep cultural and socioeconomic intelligence regarding global supply chains. It recognizes that local labor NGO reporting and worker voice channels must operate "in the languages actually spoken on the floor" and outside the control of local supervisors. It also identifies specific regional labor dynamics (e.g., debt-bonded migrant labor in specific corridors) and acknowledges that Western companies walking away from a facility the moment a journalist calls often harms vulnerable workers more than it helps them.
